module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 238

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Topology
open Set Filter Real

namespace Erdos238

/--
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (c₁ > 0) (c₂ > 0), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry

/--
It is well-known that the conjecture above is true when `c₁` is sufficiently small.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_238.variants.small_c1 : ∀ c₂ > 0, ∀ᶠ c₁ in 𝓝[>] 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in atTop, ∃ (k : ℕ),
    c₁ * log x < k ∧ ∃ f : Fin k → ℕ, ∃ m, (∀ i, f i ≤ x ∧ f i = (m + i.1).nth Nat.Prime)
    ∧ ∀ i : Fin (k - 1), c₂ < primeGap (m + i.1) := by
  sorry


end Erdos238

reformulations.difference: The gap threshold c₂ is inferred as ℕ rather than ℝ, and the statement tests only adjacent gaps instead of differences between every pair of distinct primes in the block.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Positive integers are cofinal among positive real thresholds: for any real c₂ > 0, choose a positive integer n > c₂ and apply the integer-threshold statement. The converse follows by restricting real thresholds to integers. Nat.nth Nat.Prime enumerates the primes strictly increasingly, so for i < j the difference p_j − p_i is at least the adjacent difference p_(i+1) − p_i. Thus the adjacent-gap condition is equivalent to the source's all-pairs condition. These equivalences, combined at the level of the universally quantified eventual statement, were proved in Review238.main_equiv_all_pairwise_real.

reformulations.difference: As in the main theorem, c₂ ranges over positive naturals and only adjacent gaps are tested. 'Sufficiently small positive c₁' is expressed by eventuality in the right-hand neighborhood 𝓝[>] 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same cofinal-threshold and adjacent-to-all-pairs arguments apply. The neighborhood assertion is exactly ∃ ε > 0, ∀ c₁, 0 < c₁ → c₁ < ε → P c₁. Its position after the c₂ quantifier correctly permits ε to depend on c₂, while the subsequent atTop eventuality permits the x threshold to depend on both constants. The combined equivalence was proved in Review238.small_equiv_all_pairwise_real.
